messages:
jess_support: Customer report — structured JSON mode streaming returned an incomplete object (trailing comma) midstream, their parser fails. They saw final chunk end with `,\n}` missing the last field. They've attached a minimal repro.
luca_ingest: can you paste the repro and the exact curl they used? also which edge/region? :thinking:
jess_support: pasted below from customer (redacted):\n\n```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","mode":"json","stream":true,"input":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
\nCustomer log: last 2 chunks:\n```
...\n{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"\"items\": [ {\"id\":1,\"name\": \"foo\"},"}} ,
{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"\"id\":2,\"name\": \"bar\"},"}}\n# connection closed by remote
```
jess_support: note the final brace never arrived, they see `..."},` then EOF. They said it happens ~1-2% of streams, different regions.
priya_eng: thanks. initial theory: upstream socket FIN or proxy chunk cutoff. do we have any LB logs for that customer request id? ask for request-id header if available.
jess_support: customer sent x-rw-request-id: rw-req-4567 and edge region eu-west-1
mike_infra: checking gateway traces for rw-req-4567... seeing a 499 from client at the edge 1738800128, followed by our origin connection close at 1738800130. looks like a midstream client disconnect, but their app says it didn't drop. could be an intermediary (corporate proxy / mobile carrier) cutting keepalive.
luca_ingest: is there any case where our runtime flushes a partial JSON chunk to the socket and then our upstream closes before finishing the last small write? i.e., write(2) partial boundary then SIGPIPE.
priya_eng: runtime writes are atomic at chunk level but the kernel can still report partial if network backpressure or proxy. also note some clients/HTTP libs close immediately on parsing error then we might abort.
mike_infra: edge shows TLS handshake ok; connection closed with FIN from client side. we have TCP retransmits around the end of the stream which suggest a RST or poor mobile link. recommend customer run a tcpdump or curl --trace to confirm.
jess_support: customer insists they didn't kill the connection. their stack: node-fetch inside an express server behind nginx (corporate env). they will try a direct curl from a desktop to rule out the proxy.
priya_eng: in parallel let's add more telemetry: enable streaming boundary debug for that request id (will log final chunks and send to secure bucket). mike, can you enable for eu-west-1 and link logs here?
mike_infra: deploy-bot: feature flag live, enabling stream-trace for rw-req-4567 in eu-west-1. will keep for 1 hour.
deploy-bot: feature flag stream-trace enabled for rw-req-4567 (eu-west-1).
luca_ingest: also ask customer to set `Accept: application/json-seq` or use our non-SSE streaming mode to see if chunk framing differs. suggest `curl -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' --no-buffer` vs `--raw` to compare.
jess_support: customer will try direct curl + curl --no-buffer + server-side tcpdump. asked them to share outputs.
priya_eng: if we confirm midstream closure at an intermediary, workaround options: increase client-side keepalive, set server to retry with our dedupe-id header (if idempotent), or return a structured error wrapper when we detect truncated JSON. long term we should detect incomplete structured output and append a graceful error chunk rather than leaving dangling comma.
luca_ingest: opened GH issue: "detect-truncated-json-in-streams and emit final error object" to track implementation work.
jess_support: marking as customer escalated. I'll update with customer's repro results. :phone:
